The shared targeting of this enzyme by Tiotropium and Irigenin implies a possible role in the regulation of cGMP levels, which could affect receptor function. The integration of these pathways highlights a possible pharmacological interaction where Tiotropium may exert its effects through a cGMP-dependent mechanism, indirectly influencing the 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 2B. The evidence supports a plausible link between Tiotropium and the 5-hydroxytryptamine receptor 2B, though the exact mechanism of interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
